text:
alicia.m: heads up — planning a graceful restart window in az4 this friday 02:00-05:00 UTC to mitigate thermal drift on a subset of T4/T4x racks. will do staggered reboots + quick egress validation.

jordan.k: ETA on number of nodes affected?

alicia.m: ~18 gpu nodes across pool 'infer-az4-p1' (~10% of regional capacity). each reboot takes ~6-8m including kube drain/evict, plus 10m cooldown. overall plan: batch of 3 nodes every 15m.

sam.r: do we have backfill capacity in eu-west to route burst traffic during drain? cost impact?

alicia.m: we've got ~25% spare in eu-west but routing will increase cross-region egress. ballpark extra egress cost: small for short window but will monitor. ops-bot: automatically creating short-lived route policy 'az4-maint-2026-03-20' and tagging affected pools.

lee.t: any risk of BGP flaps when we bring back NICs? last time a firmware patch caused transient routes to withdraw for ~30s.

alicia.m: good call — we'll run a BGP sanity test immediately after each node comes back. test steps will be run by deploy-bot.

deploy-bot: preflight checks passed: kernel/drivers look compatible on 18/18 nodes. will execute `bgp-sanity --peer all --timeout 10s` after each reboot.

nora.s: can we add a short acceptance probe for model latency (p95) hitting each warmed node after join? if p95 > 300ms we should failback.

alicia.m: yes — plan: run the probe against a canary endpoint, threshold 300ms p95, 5 samples over 30s. failback policy = move traffic off node and mark for manual inspection.

jordan.k: share exact schedule so support can staff. also list contact for escalation.

alicia.m: schedule snapshot: 02:00 UTC batch A (nodes 1-3), 02:30 batch B (4-6), 02:45 batch C (7-9), 03:00 batch D (10-12), 03:30 batch E (13-15), 04:00 batch F (16-18). oncall: @nora.s primary, @lee.t secondary. slack channel #eng-infra will post updates, pager if BGP failure.

sam.r: does autoscaler need config change to avoid rapid backfills?

alicia.m: set autoscale.cooldown to 900s for the window (will patch at 01:50 UTC). snippet: ```yaml
autoscaler:
  cool_down: 900s
  max_unavailable: 5
```

ops-bot: patch applied to cluster 'az4' at 01:52 UTC by alicia.m.

jordan.k: any opt-in for dedicated customers pinned to infer-az4-p1? they may see slower provisioning.

alicia.m: customers with dedicated capacity won't be impacted; pinned pools are isolated. only shared pool workloads will be rerouted. we will post a status update to the customer dashboard and #customer-success 30m before.

nora.s: I'll own the BGP probe and latency probe dashboards during the window. will escalate to network on first sign of >2 route withdraws or p95 breach.

lee.t: suggest running a quick NVME health check pre-reboot (simple SMART) — if any disk shows early failure, take node out of rotation permanently.

alicia.m: agreed — adding `nvme-smartctl -a /dev/nvme0n1` to preflight. ops-bot will attach results to the incident ticket.

deploy-bot: dry-run: `kubectl drain node/gpu-node-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=600s` (no evictions triggered in dry-run).

jordan.k: looks solid. timeline shared with support and sales. I added a note to the maintenance calendar. :thumbsup:

alicia.m: thanks all — will post final confirmation 30m before start. if anyone sees unexpected capacity pressure before then ping here. 

ops-bot: maintenance ticket created: MNT-214000-az4-thermals. link: https://ops.example/redwood/issues/MNT-214000
